highlights: Today now flags stretches of wet-leaf weather — long spells when foliage stays wet at mild temperatures, which is what foliar diseases need to get going. It is a prompt to go and look at the susceptible crops, not a diagnosis, and it stays quiet on about three days in four.

Cool-night warnings now cover the 45-50F range. There was a warning below 45F and another below 40F but nothing in between, so the first two chilly nights of the season passed without a word while sweet potatoes and okra were still out. Chilling damage starts well above freezing.
